Remark
[local conformal flatness and isothermal coordinates]

Source: petersen:page-0176 ↗ prop:pet-ch4-snk-constant-curvature 1. ch4:4.7.17A metric is locally conformally flat if near every point $g=e^{-2\psi } ig((dx^1)^2+\dots +(dx^n)^2 ig)$. (1) Show the space forms $S^n_k$, $dr^2+\mathrm{sn}_k^2(r)ds_{n-1}^2$, are locally conformally flat. (2) Show a locally conformally flat Einstein metric has constant curvature. (3) For $\dim M=2$ (Gauss's isothermal coordinates): (a) if $du e 0$ on $O\subset M$, show there is, up to sign, a unique $1$-form $\omega =i_{ abla u}\mathrm{vol}_g$ with $|du|=|\omega |$ and $d(du,\omega )=0$; (b) show $d\omega =(\Delta _gu)\mathrm{vol}_g$; (c) show isothermal coordinates exist near $p$ whenever there is a harmonic $u$ near $p$ with $du|_p e 0$.
